To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. The performance of the FPGAs is comparable to the performance of a graphics chip.

the performance of a shader implemented on a Virtex-II FPGA is comparable to a shader implemented on an ATI R420 GPU, and that a shader implemented on the FPGA is 2-3x faster than a shader implemented on software.
1. FPGAs are not suitable to implement pixel shaders. They are too slow and too power hungry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: • How well do modern FPGAs support the graphics shader model? • What are the limitations of the graphics shader model when it is mapped onto FPGAs?
the following issues: • What are the similarities and differences between FPGAs and graphics chips?

1) the implementation of graphics shaders on a finegrained, high-performance FPGA, and the comparison with graphics shaders running on graphics processors, and 2) the implementation of an FPGA graphics processor using a coarse-grained FPGA, and the evaluation of its performance and flexibility.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of a fine-grained FPGA is not as good as that of a modern GPU.
the FPGA implementation is faster and more power efficient than the GPU.
the performance and flexibility of FPGAs are not sufficient for the implementation of the vertex shader stage, but are sufficient for the implementation the pixel shader stage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to implement a pixel shader in hardware using FPGAs.
we were able to show that FPGAs can indeed be used to implement graphics shaders, and that the resulting performance is very close to that of a graphics chip.
the FPGAs can be a viable alternative for implementing graphics shaders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FPGA implementation is much more flexible and can be used to accelerate a wide range of applications.
FPGAs can be used to efficiently and flexibly implement graphics shader pipelines, with performance and energy consumption that is comparable to that of a modern graphics chip.
FPGAs are a viable and competitive alternative for implementing pixel shader stages.
